title: Confluence vs Trello
description: A workflow-fit guide to Confluence and Trello. The product profiles place them in Productivity and Project Management, respectively, so this is not a like-for-like feature ranking. Compare project execution, task ownership, dependencies, deadlines, and status with documentation, decisions, and reusable team knowledge. Decide whether one tool or an integrated pair best fits the actual workflow.
verdict: Neither Confluence nor Trello is a universal winner because the product profiles cover different work needs. Identify whether the main friction is planning tasks, assigning owners, tracking dependencies, and meeting deadlines, or keeping decisions, specifications, and shared knowledge findable. Test a real project from planning through handoff, confirm permissions and search behavior, and check whether the tools link work without duplicate records.

faqs.question: Are Confluence and Trello direct substitutes?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Their profiles list different primary categories (Productivity and Project Management). Compare the actual job each must do; they may be alternatives for a narrow workflow or complementary products.

faqs.question: When should I evaluate Confluence?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Confluence when its primary role in Productivity matches your must-have workflow. Test the relevant tasks and verify current capabilities, plan limits, permissions, and terms with the vendor.

faqs.question: When should I evaluate Trello?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Trello when its primary role in Project Management matches your requirement. Confirm it handles the workflow end to end, including handoffs, reporting, access controls, and data export.

faqs.question: Can the products be used together?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if they cover different steps. Verify current integration documentation, the data exchanged, sync frequency, permissions, error handling, and any connector fees before relying on a connection.

faqs.question: How should I compare total cost?
faqs.answer: Include seats, usage limits, add-ons, implementation, training, administration, integration maintenance, and switching costs—not just advertised starting prices.

faqs.question: Does this page name a verified winner?
faqs.answer: No. This is a workflow decision guide, not an independently verified head-to-head score. The stored winner and feature rows are not verified; test your requirements and confirm current details with each vendor.
